app.description: App this context belongs to. Not required (a design may cover an app the extractor could not resolve), but sdet-plan-generator keys off it to match contexts for a run, so omitting it in a multi-app split defeats the split.

design_source.description: Provenance of the Figma export this context was extracted from — copied verbatim from the Export Design Raw JSON plugin envelope. Lets a reviewer tell a full-page export from a partial selection export without re-opening Figma.

scope.description: envelope scope. 'selection' means flows leaving the selected layers are not in the export, so ui_flow coverage cannot be verified.

truncated_count.description: envelope export.truncatedCount. Non-zero means the depth cap dropped children — elements below those layers were never exported.

truncated_nodes.description: envelope export.truncatedNodes (up to 20 samples) — the layers worth flattening before the next export.

extraction_status.description: How much of the source document was captured. COMPLETE = everything the document specified was captured. PARTIAL = the document did not specify some things, so they were left empty and listed in extraction_notes; this is the normal result for a work-in-progress doc and is not an error. LIMITED = a config file, schema or the validator was unavailable, so part of the run had less grounding than usual — see extraction_notes. Not COMPLETE whenever extraction_notes is non-empty.

extraction_notes.description: Things the source document did not say, recorded instead of guessing a value. An empty array means nothing was left open. A non-empty array is normal and expected on a work-in-progress document — it is a to-do list for the author, not a list of errors.

field.description: JSON path of the field left empty, e.g. business_requirements[3].target_module. Use 'ENVIRONMENT' for tool or install issues not tied to one field.

reason.description: What was checked and what was found there, e.g. 'PRD section 4.2 states the rule but names no module'.

action.description: The concrete next step, e.g. 'confirm the target module with the PM'.

follow_up.description: How much attention this needs. NEEDS_ANSWER = someone has to supply this before the tests can cover it. WORTH_CHECKING = a value was produced, but without its usual reference source, so confirm it. FYI = optional content the document simply does not have; no action needed.

visual_analysis_scratchpad.description: Write a 2-3 sentence overview of what you detect in the export before compiling the technical fields. List screens found. Note: the export carries no geometry or styling, so this is a structural reading of names, variants and reactions — not a visual one.

overall_ambiguity_rating.description: HIGH = a screen or trigger element could not be resolved. MEDIUM = flows resolved, but through fallbacks/inference. LOW = every ui_flow edge is EXPLICIT and every layer name convention-compliant.

convention_compliance.description: Tallies of how well the export follows the design team's five flow-authoring conventions. This is the feedback loop back to design — a high inferred/unresolved count means the next export needs fixing at source, not more guessing downstream.

connectors_total.description: Every CONNECTOR node in the export. Must equal the sum of the buckets below plus note connectors plus connector-derived blockers.

connectors_resolved_to_screen.description: Standard #1 followed: the connector ends on a screen frame.

connectors_inferred_to_screen.description: Standard #1 not followed: the destination was an element, and the screen was inferred from its ancestors.

connectors_unresolvable.description: Floating endpoint, orphaned node id, or an intra-screen connector that is neither a flow nor a note.

note_connectors.description: Standard #5: TEXT-to-FRAME connectors whose text starts with Note or Context.

reactions_with_destination.description: Standard #2 followed: a tap-family reaction naming a destination.

reactions_without_destination.description: Standard #2 not followed: tap trigger with a null/absent destination. Each is also a blocking_issues entry.

unlabelled_branches.description: Standard #4 not followed: a trigger element with 2+ outgoing connectors and no connector labels to discriminate them.

non_descriptive_names.description: Standard #3 not followed: frames/layers named Frame 427, Group 12, Rectangle, Blue Button, etc.

unreachable_screens.description: Screen frames in no ui_flow edge and no flowStartingPoints entry.

screen_id.description: Figma frame name with any trailing state qualifier stripped, forced into UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. 'Approve Disbursement — Error' -> APPROVE_DISBURSEMENT)

source_ref.description: Figma node id of the screen frame (e.g. '2015:31162'), so a reviewer can jump straight to it.

deep_link.description: Deep link that opens this screen, taken from a prototype URL action matching the app config's deeplink_scheme, or stated in a Note/Context annotation. Absent when the design does not state one — never construct a plausible URI. sdet-plan-generator uses this both as the deep_link_nav category trigger and as a navigation shortcut in preference to a full UI walk.

entry_point.description: True when this frame is named in the page's flowStartingPoints[] — i.e. the designer marked it as a prototype flow entry.

flow_name.description: Name of the prototype flow this screen starts, from flowStartingPoints[].name.

screen_states.description: The designer's own wording for each state, kept verbatim (e.g. 'Promo Applying (loading)').

state_kinds.description: screen_states normalised to a fixed vocabulary. This is what makes downstream category selection deterministic — sdet-plan-generator fires negative_error / offline / theming_darkmode / localization_regional / permission triggers off these values rather than pattern-matching free text. Keep both fields: screen_states is the source of truth for wording, state_kinds for machine decisions.

element_id.description: Built from the app config's naming_convention.element_id_pattern and role_vocabulary: <SCREEN_ID>.<purpose><role_suffix>, optionally .<state> (e.g. APPROVE_DISBURSEMENT.approve_btn, HISTORY_PAGE.affiliator_search_input). Screen id is UPPER_SNAKE; the role half is lower_snake, matching the config's role_vocabulary casing and the developer's locator names.

source_ref.description: Figma node id of this layer.

type.description: Free-text type as read from the design (Figma node type plus the design's role token).

role.description: Normalised role, from the layer's role token (standard #3). Machine-readable companion to `type`: sdet-plan-generator uses it to decide whether a screen is interactive (INPUT/TOGGLE/DROPDOWN/SLIDER/CAROUSEL) for the interruption_lifecycle and a11y_baseline triggers, instead of pattern-matching free text.

accessibility_id.description: Accessibility / test id the designer wrote into a Dev Mode annotation, transcribed verbatim. This is the design half of the locator handoff: sdet-plan-generator's element_locator_handoff joins it to the real per-platform locator that code-change-extractor reports. Absent when the design does not state one — never derive it from the layer name.

platform_hints.description: Per-platform ids when the annotation states them separately. Populate only from what the annotation says; omit the whole object otherwise. Never a placeholder or an 'UNRESOLVED' string.

trigger.description: The reaction's trigger.type (ON_CLICK, ON_PRESS, AFTER_TIMEOUT, ...) or the designer's own wording.

element_ambiguity.description: Per-element confidence, when this element specifically is less certain than the screen overall.

trigger_element_id.description: The element that triggers the transition. Absent for a frame-to-frame connector with no identifiable trigger element — omit it rather than inventing a token, and say so in blocking_issues.

condition.description: The connector's label (standard #4), or the conditional block's condition. Empty string means unconditional.

navigation_kind.description: What kind of transition this is. SWAP / CHANGE_TO / SCROLL_TO reactions are element state changes, not navigation, and never appear as ui_flow edges.

edge_source.description: Where the edge came from. The _INFERRED variants mean a design convention was not followed and the destination screen (or trigger element) was derived by walking ancestors — each has a matching WORTH_CHECKING extraction_note.

source_ref.description: Figma node id of the connector, or of the node carrying the reaction.
